fields.why: any program can use the kernel's virtual machine code; bugs there (Januscape, CVE-2026-53359) turn that into root. Only the kvm group needs it

fields.why: any user can make the kernel load old serial-line modules, a recurring source of root exploits; nothing on a desktop needs it

events.text: /dev/kvm is 0604 (every account): any program can use the kernel's virtual machine code; bugs there (Januscape, CVE-2026-53359) turn that into root. Only the kvm group needs it

fields.fix: printf 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0660"\n' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/65-kvm.rules && sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER && sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger -s misc (sign out and in again so the new group applies; virtual machines keep working)
fields.why: any program can use the kernel's virtual machine code; bugs there (Januscape, CVE-2026-53359) turn that into root. Only the kvm group needs it

events.text: kernel.kptr_restrict = : kernel addresses are not hidden from programs without the syslog right in every case, and a known address helps an exploit aim; 1 hides them from those programs, root still sees them

fields.fix: echo 'kernel.kptr_restrict = 1' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/60-heimdall-hardening.conf && sudo sysctl -w kernel.kptr_restrict=1
fields.why: kernel addresses are not hidden from programs without the syslog right in every case, and a known address helps an exploit aim; 1 hides them from those programs, root still sees them

events.text: fs.protected_regular = 10: programs can be tricked into writing to a planted file in shared folders like /tmp

fields.fix: echo 'fs.protected_regular = 2' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/60-heimdall-hardening.conf && sudo sysctl -w fs.protected_regular=2
fields.why: programs can be tricked into writing to a planted file in shared folders like /tmp

events.text: kvm_intel nested=Y: a guest can run its own hypervisor on this one, the path most KVM escapes (Januscape among them) need; only VMs inside VMs use it

fields.fix: echo 'options kvm_intel nested=0' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/60-heimdall-nested.conf (applies at the next restart; undo by deleting the file)
fields.why: a guest can run its own hypervisor on this one, the path most KVM escapes (Januscape among them) need; only VMs inside VMs use it

events.text: /dev/kvm is 0604 (every account): any program can use the kernel's virtual machine code; bugs there (Januscape, CVE-2026-53359) turn that into root. Only the kvm group needs it

fields.fix: printf 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0660"\n' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/65-kvm.rules && sudo usermod -aG kvm $USER && sudo udevadm control --reload && sudo udevadm trigger -s misc (sign out and in again so the new group applies; virtual machines keep working)
fields.why: any program can use the kernel's virtual machine code; bugs there (Januscape, CVE-2026-53359) turn that into root. Only the kvm group needs it
